label: Copy phase, mid-to-late recall, input is one of 0/1/z/x/e/c/f/n
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never during the original tokens or on <DEL>, and almost never on the first two outputs (recall_idx 0-1). The rate peaks around recall_idx 3-5 and grows with L. Which token is input (the token just copied back) matters a lot: 0 (rate 28%), 1, z, x, e, c, f, n are strongly preferred, and o, h, w, 2 and most other letters rarely trigger it. Activation is higher when several of these preferred tokens come in a row or earlier in the sequence (n_seen of the set >= 3 raises precision to about 0.56), and when the token being output is also in the set. It is also more likely in sequences with more digits. The top activations sit on a 0 in the middle of a run of preferred tokens. The predicate captures about 90% of activation mass, but precision is about 0.46 because the neuron is also gated by this accumulated context, which a simple predicate does not capture.
